universalLicenseRecognitionStatus.notes: CONFIRMED — Virginia separately offers Universal License Recognition (ULR) as a distinct, broader pathway for out-of-state licensees generally, per DPOR's own homepage/Applicants page. This is a genuinely SEPARATE mechanism from the 3 named bilateral reciprocal agreements below (Kentucky/Maryland/West Virginia) — an applicant from a state NOT on the bilateral list may still have a real ULR pathway, not covered by this record's reciprocityRules field. Not conflated with, or used to broaden, the bilateral agreement list.

compactMembership.notes: Virginia's electrician reciprocity operates via named bilateral agreements and ULR — neither is a single multistate compact license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact). Recorded as false to avoid conflating these real mechanisms with a compact under this field's actual schema meaning.

reciprocityRules.value: Virginia has real, named bilateral reciprocal examination agreements for the Master Electrician license with exactly three states: Kentucky (Master <-> VA Master), Maryland (Master Electrical Tradesman <-> VA Master — Master-only, this agreement does not cover Journeyman), and West Virginia (Master <-> VA Master). A separate Universal License Recognition (ULR) pathway may independently apply to applicants from other states — see universalLicenseRecognitionStatus.
